les: Wat kinders gevra het en wat elke kind toekom

items.bewering: Gesproke woorde kan vergeet word of anders onthou word. Die opgeskrewe eise bly staan, en enigeen kan gaan kyk wat presies gevra is.
items.bron: Memory research summarised in the SAGE Encyclopedia of Theory in Psychology entry 'memory as reconstructive' (sk.sagepub.com) and in summaries of Bartlett (1932). Recall of something heard or read shortens and gets distorted over time. A written text can be consulted unchanged.

items.bewering: Hulle lys is 'n handves.
items.bron: The document is titled 'The Children's Charter of South Africa' and is a list of articles of demands (charter text reproduced at naturalchild.org/advocacy/childrens_charter.html; SAHO, sahistory.org.za/article/childrens-charter).

items.bewering: In 1992 het meer as 200 kinders uit streke regoor Suid-Afrika in die Kaap saamgekom.
items.bron: SAHO (sahistory.org.za/article/childrens-charter): summit 'held in Cape Town in 1992', 'attended by over 200 children'. AAM Archives pro25 (aamarchives.org): 'over 200 children', Cape Town, June 1992. The charter's About section puts it at Somerset West and names 17 regions in the preamble (20 in the About text). Either way it was in the Cape and from regions across the country.

items.bewering: Hulle was by 'n internasionale beraad oor kinders se regte.
items.bron: Charter text: written by 'the delegates of the International Children's Summit held from 27 May to 1 June 1992' (naturalchild.org). Mail & Guardian / SAHRC, 'Twenty-five years of children's rights' (mg.co.za, 2014): part of the 1992 International Conference on the Rights of Children in South Africa.

items.bewering: Grootmense het die beraad gereël en die kinders gehelp.
items.bron: Mail & Guardian / SAHRC (mg.co.za, 2014): the summit was part of a conference hosted by the University of the Western Cape's Community Law Centre and facilitated by Molo Songololo.

items.bewering: Die kinders self het die woorde van die Kinderhandves van Suid-Afrika geskryf.
items.bron: Charter text names its authors as 'the delegates of the International Children's Summit', and those delegates were the children (naturalchild.org). SAHO: 'drawn up at the end of the summit'. AAM Archives: the children 'set out demands'.

items.bewering: Op 1 Junie 1992 het hulle dit aan die einde van die beraad aanvaar.
items.bron: Charter text: summit 27 May to 1 June 1992, charter approved 1 June 1992 (naturalchild.org). SAHO: drawn up 'at the end of the summit'. AAM Archives: June 1992.

items.bewering: Die handves is nie 'n wet nie maar 'n lys van wat kinders eis.
items.bron: The charter is a summit declaration of the children's needs and demands (SAHO; AAM Archives: 'set out demands to be fed in to the negotiations'). It was never enacted, and the Constitution's s28 is the binding text (source.acts.co.za, s28).

items.bewering: Die kinders wou hê dat daardie eise die onderhandelinge oor 'n nuwe Grondwet moet bereik.
items.bron: AAM Archives pro25: the children 'set out demands to be fed in to the negotiations for a new South African constitution'. Charter preamble complains that children were not on the agenda 'within the CODESA negotiations', and its resolutions ask that 'the future constitution and bill of rights' include special provisions for children (naturalchild.org).

items.bewering: Elke kind moet van sy geboorte af 'n naam en 'n nasionaliteit kry.
items.blok: Wat die kinders onder meer gevra het
items.bron: Charter Part II Art. 2: 'All children have the right to a name and nationality as soon as they are born.' (naturalchild.org)

items.bewering: Elke kind mag sy eie geloof, kultuur of oortuiging uitleef.
items.blok: Wat die kinders onder meer gevra het
items.bron: Charter Part II Art. 4: 'All children have the right to freedom to practice their own religion, culture or beliefs without fear.' (naturalchild.org)

items.bewering: Elke kind mag sy mening gee en gehoor word.
items.blok: Wat die kinders onder meer gevra het
items.bron: Charter Part II Art. 3: children have the right to express their own opinions and to be heard in matters affecting them (naturalchild.org).

items.bewering: Voorbeeld: die onderwyser vra wat die klas van 'n nuwe reël dink, sy dink oor elke mening na en sê waarom die reël bly of verander; gehoor word beteken dat jou mening werklik oorweeg word, nie dat jy altyd jou sin kry nie.
items.blok: Wat die kinders onder meer gevra het
items.bron: UNCRC Art. 12 and CRC General Comment No. 12 (hrlibrary.umn.edu/crc/gencom12.html; chr.up.ac.za copy): a child's views must be given 'due weight' and considered, which is not the same as the child deciding. The mapping holds: the teacher weighs every opinion and gives a reason, and the outcome may still go against the child. A learner reasoning further from it will not conclude that being heard means getting one's way.

items.bewering: Die handves vra 'n veilige gesin wat vir 'n kind sorg.
items.blok: Wat die handves nog verder sê
items.bron: Charter Part II Art. 6: 'All children have the right to a safe, secure and nurturing family.' (naturalchild.org)

items.bewering: Geen kind mag gedwing word om op straat te leef nie.
items.blok: Wat die handves nog verder sê

items.bewering: Kinders moet teen kinderarbeid beskerm word.
items.blok: Wat die handves nog verder sê
items.bron: Charter Part II Art. 9 calls for a minimum age of employment and protection from exploitative labour that harms children's health or education (naturalchild.org).

items.bewering: Die handves vra verpligte skool wat gratis en gelyk is.
items.blok: Wat die handves nog verder sê
items.bron: Charter Part II Art. 8: 'All children have the right to free and equal, non-racial, non-sexist and compulsory education within one department.' (naturalchild.org)

items.bewering: 'n Kind wat snags koors kry, het meestal 'n grootmens nodig en soms ook 'n kliniek.
items.blok: Wat die handves nog verder sê
items.bron: Mayo Clinic Health System, 'Fever in children' (communityhealth.mayoclinic.org) and Cleveland Clinic (health.clevelandclinic.org, 'Kids' fevers: when to worry'): most childhood fevers are viral and can be cared for at home by a caregiver, and medical care is needed for warning signs, a very high fever, a long fever or a young infant. As an example of health care, the mapping holds: the 'meestal' adult, 'soms' clinic split matches that guidance.

items.bewering: Die handves kla dat kinders daardie sorg kortkom.
items.blok: Wat die handves nog verder sê
items.bron: Charter Part I Art. 2: 'Children do not receive proper health and medical care and attention, yet do not have the right to demand treatment.' (naturalchild.org). 'Daardie sorg' (the adult's attention and the clinic) matches 'health and medical care and attention'.

items.bewering: Lees die Grondwet se deel oor kinders langs die handves en jy sien baie van dieselfde dinge. Die kinders het nie die Grondwet geskryf nie, maar hulle het baie van daardie dinge gevra.
items.blok: Die handves en die Grondwet langs mekaar
items.bron: Compared Constitution s28(1)(a)-(f) (source.acts.co.za) with Charter Part II (naturalchild.org). Name and nationality from birth, family care, protection from abuse and neglect, and protection from exploitative labour appear in both. The lesson rightly claims overlap and no causal authorship.

items.bewering: Die Grondwet gee kinders ook regte buite hierdie deel.
items.blok: Die handves en die Grondwet langs mekaar
items.bron: Constitution s7(1): the Bill of Rights enshrines the rights of all people in the country. Rights such as s10 dignity, s12(1)(c) freedom from violence and s29(1)(a) basic education are held by 'everyone', children included (en.wikisource.org, Constitution 1996 Chapter 2).

items.bewering: Wat hierdie deel gee, is 'n reg en nie 'n guns nie.
items.blok: Die handves en die Grondwet langs mekaar
items.bron: Section 28 sits in the Bill of Rights. Under s7(2) 'The state must respect, protect, promote and fulfil the rights in the Bill of Rights' (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2; NWU repository paper citing s7(2)).

items.bewering: 'n Kind se voeding en skuiling is in die eerste plek sy gesin se plig. Die staat moet help waar die gesin dit nie kan doen nie.
items.blok: Die handves en die Grondwet langs mekaar
items.bron: Government of the RSA v Grootboom (CC, 2000). Per the Wikipedia case article and law-review commentary (za.vlex.com, 'The Grootboom judgment, interpretative manoeuvring...'), the Court read s28(1)(b)-(c) as placing the primary duty on parents and family, with the state's duty arising where family or parental care is lacking. Commentators criticise this reading, but it is the Court's.

items.blok: Wat die Grondwet onder meer vir elke kind gee
items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(a): 'to a name and a nationality from birth' (source.acts.co.za/constitution-of-the-republic-of-south-africa-act-1996/28__children.php).

items.bewering: sorg by sy gesin, en gepaste ander sorg as hy daaruit weggeneem word

items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(b): 'to family care or parental care, or to appropriate alternative care when removed from the family environment' (source.acts.co.za).

items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(c): 'to basic nutrition, shelter, basic health care services and social services' (source.acts.co.za).

items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(d): 'to be protected from maltreatment, neglect, abuse or degradation' (source.acts.co.za).

items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(e), 'to be protected from exploitative labour practices', and s28(1)(f)(i), work that is 'inappropriate for a person of that child's age' (source.acts.co.za).

items.blok: Wat die Grondwet onder meer vir elke kind gee
items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(f)(ii): work that would 'place at risk the child's well-being, education, physical or mental health or spiritual, moral or social development' (source.acts.co.za).

items.bewering: beskerming wat geld al wil hy self sulke werk doen
items.blok: Wat die Grondwet onder meer vir elke kind gee
items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(f): 'not to be required or permitted to perform work'. The word 'permitted' means the protection holds even when the child wants to do the work (source.acts.co.za).

items.bewering: Jou eie reg om te leer bring 'n verantwoordelikheid mee ... Jy kom skool toe, jy luister en jy doen jou werk.
items.bron: DBE, Bill of Responsibilities for the Youth of South Africa (gov.za/node/538114; gov.za/node/537982). The right to education places on learners the responsibility to attend school regularly, cooperate respectfully with teachers and fellow learners, and follow the school's rules. The breuke example, where tomorrow's work builds on today's, is a sound illustration of why attendance matters.

items.bewering: Voorbeeld: kinders gooi papier in die klas rond en niemand hoor die onderwyser nie; jy mag nie die klas se leertyd wegneem nie (ander verantwoordelikhede beskerm die regte van kinders om jou).
items.bron: Constitution s29(1)(a): everyone has the right to a basic education (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2). The DBE Bill of Responsibilities asks learners to cooperate respectfully with fellow learners (gov.za/node/538114). The mapping holds: disrupting the lesson takes from other learners' exercise of their right.

items.bewering: Voorbeeld: een kind keer elke dag 'n kleiner kind voor en dreig hom; die kleiner kind se reg om veilig te wees word nie nagekom nie. Jy mag niemand boelie nie, en jy moet praat wanneer dit gebeur.
items.bron: Constitution s12(1)(c): the right 'to be free from all forms of violence from either public or private sources' (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2). Children's Act 38 of 2005 s1 lists 'bullying by another child' as abuse (knowledgehub.health.gov.za mandatory-reporting guide). The mapping holds.

items.bewering: 'n Reg staan op papier, maar dit gebeur nie altyd vanself nie. Word jou reg nie nagekom nie, vertel 'n volwassene wat jy vertrou. Help daardie mens jou nie, vertel iemand anders totdat iemand help. 'n Kind hoef nie te wag totdat 'n grootmens begin praat nie.
items.blok: As 'n reg nie nagekom word nie
items.bron: This is standard child-protection guidance: tell an adult you trust, and keep telling until it stops. Sources: Thinkuknow / CEOP (thinkuknow.co.uk 'asking for help'); BCP Council 'Speak out, keep telling' (fid.bcpcouncil.gov.uk); Rhodes University CPAF child-protection comic ('tell ... an adult you trust').

items.bewering: Die Kinderhandves is die lys eise wat Suid-Afrikaanse kinders in 1992 self opgestel het. Dit is nie 'n wet nie, en dit staan nie in die Grondwet nie.
items.bron: SAHO and AAM Archives (see above). The Constitution's s28 is its own text, and the charter is not reproduced in the Constitution (source.acts.co.za s28).

items.bewering: Die naam 'handves' word ook vir ander dokumente gebruik, en in party van hulle staan reëls wat wel in die land geld.
items.bron: The Bill of Rights, Chapter 2 of the Constitution, is called the 'Handves van Regte' in Afrikaans legal writing, for example Buchner-Eveleigh & Nienaber, PER 2012 (law.nwu.ac.za) and the NWU repository paper. It is binding law.

items.bewering: beraad: 'n Groot vergadering waar mense oor een belangrike saak saampraat.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English, entry 'bosberaad' (dsae.co.za/entry/bosberaad/e01130): beraad means 'deliberation, consultation', and a bosberaad is a meeting to deliberate on difficult issues. The 1992 event is called a 'Summit' in English.

items.bewering: Grondwet: Die hoogste wet van die land, waarby elke ander wet moet hou. Elke ander reël wat in die land geld en alles wat die staat doen, moet ook daarby hou.
items.bron: Constitution s2: 'This Constitution is the supreme law of the Republic; law or conduct inconsistent with it is invalid' (acts.co.za, s2 Supremacy of Constitution).

items.bewering: wet: 'n Reël wat die Parlement, 'n provinsiale wetgewer of 'n munisipale raad vir sy eie gebied maak. Dit geld vir mense in daardie gebied, en die staat kan dit afdwing. Nie al die reëls van 'n land staan in wette nie: 'n minister maak ook reëls onder 'n wet, en party reëls kom uit hofbeslissings of uit ou gebruike.
items.bron: Constitution s43 vests legislative authority in Parliament (national), the provincial legislatures and the Municipal Councils (local) (acts.co.za s43; PER/PELJ commentary at scielo.org.za). Ministerial regulations under an Act, common law developed by courts, and customary law are standard parts of SA law, and Constitution s8(1) refers to the Bill of Rights applying to 'all law'.

items.bewering: nasionaliteit: Nasionaliteit sê aan watter land 'n mens behoort.
items.bron: European Convention on Nationality Art. 2(a), as cited in de Groot (law.yale.edu): nationality is 'the legal bond between a person and a State'. USLegal: the legal relationship between a person and a state. A simplification, but it is accurate.

items.bewering: reg: Iets waarop 'n mens geregtig is en wat die wet beskerm. Sommige regte staan in die Grondwet; ander kom onder meer uit gewone wette, uit ou gebruike, of uit 'n ooreenkoms. Die staat moet die regte in die Handves van Regte eerbiedig en beskerm, en ander mense en maatskappye mag party regte ook nie aantas nie.
items.bron: Constitution s7(2), 'The state must respect, protect, promote and fulfil the rights in the Bill of Rights', and s8(2), 'A provision of the Bill of Rights binds a natural or a juristic person if, and to the extent that, it is applicable' (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2). 'Party regte' correctly reflects 'to the extent that it is applicable'.

items.bewering: Net 'n regsreël mag 'n reg in die Handves van Regte beperk. Die beperking moet ook redelik wees, en 'n mens moet kan verduidelik hoekom dit nodig is.
items.bron: Constitution s36(1): 'The rights in the Bill of Rights may be limited only in terms of law of general application', to the extent that the limitation is reasonable and justifiable, taking into account its purpose and whether less restrictive means exist (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2). The lesson leaves out the 'general application' requirement, which is a simplification and not a falsehood.

items.bewering: regsreël: 'n Reël wat in die land geld, soos 'n wet, 'n reël wat die regering onder 'n wet maak, of 'n ou gebruik.
items.bron: Consistent with s36(1) 'law of general application', which covers legislation, delegated legislation, common law and customary law (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2). The examples follow 'soos' and do not form a closed list.

items.bewering: verantwoordelikheid: Iets wat jy moet doen en waarvoor jy moet antwoord. Sommige verantwoordelikhede beskerm ander mense se regte; ander kom saam met jou eie reg.
items.bron: DBE Bill of Responsibilities for the Youth of South Africa (gov.za/node/538114) pairs each right with the responsibility it brings, such as attending school for the right to education, and with respect for others' rights.

items.bewering: kinderarbeid: Werk deur kinders wat hulle skade doen, wat hulle uit die skool hou, of waarvoor hulle nog te jonk is.
items.bron: ILO definition as reproduced by Humanium and the Open Risk Manual: work that is harmful to physical and mental development and interferes with schooling. ILO Convention 138 sets minimum ages for work. Also Constitution s28(1)(e)-(f).

items.bewering: uitbuit: Om 'n kind vir jou eie voordeel te gebruik en hom onregverdig te behandel, onder meer deur sy werk, sy liggaam of sy nood te gebruik.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005: s1 'abuse' includes 'a labour practice that exploits a child', and s150(1) lists a child who is exploited, trafficked or sold among children in need of care (acts.co.za s150; knowledgehub.health.gov.za reporting guide). Work, the body (sexual exploitation) and the child's need are the recognised forms. The ordinary sense of 'exploit' is to use unfairly for one's own benefit.

items.bewering: mishandeling: Mishandeling is wanneer iemand 'n kind verkeerd of wreed behandel.
items.bron: 'Mishandeling' corresponds to 'maltreatment' in Constitution s28(1)(d) (source.acts.co.za), meaning cruel or wrongful treatment. The definition is broad and accurate.

items.bewering: verwaarlosing: Wanneer die mense wat vir 'n kind moet sorg, nie doen wat hulle moet nie, sodat hy nie die basiese dinge kry wat hy nodig het nie, onder meer kos, klere, veiligheid, aandag, hulp wanneer hy siek is, en skool.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005 s1: neglect is 'a failure in the exercise of parental responsibilities to provide for the child's basic physical, intellectual, emotional or social needs' (quoted in the socialwork.journals.ac.za article and the acts.co.za 'neglect' entry). Practitioner indicators list food, clothing, medical care, schooling, shelter and supervision (news.nwu.ac.za 'Protecting our children').

items.bewering: Armoede alleen is nie verwaarlosing nie.
items.bron: Could not settle this. The Children's Act s1 definition ('a failure in the exercise of parental responsibilities to provide for the child's basic ... needs') has no exclusion for poverty, and s150 contains no poverty provision (acts.co.za s150, read in full). The SA Law Reform Commission's child-care review (Discussion Paper, ch. 10 'Child protection', ci.uct.ac.za/media/106744, p. 327) treats 'neglect which occurs because caregivers lack the resources to meet the child's needs' as one recognised kind of neglect, alongside neglect despite resources. Secondary SA summaries say only that poverty alone is not a sufficient reason to REMOVE a child, which is a narrower claim. The flat definitional statement is a widely held child-protection principle, but I found no authoritative SA source for it, and one authoritative SA source frames resource-driven deprivation as neglect. A person should decide whether to keep it, narrow it to what is sourced (that a family's poverty on its own is not a reason to take a child away), or cut it. The entry's first sentence ('nie doen wat hulle moet nie') already carries most of the protective intent.

items.bewering: misbruik: skade of slegte behandeling wat iemand met opset aan 'n kind doen; slaan, skop en ander opsetlike besering; seksuele misbruik, en ook wanneer 'n grootmens weet en toelaat dat iemand dit doen; boelie, ook deur 'n ander kind; werk waarmee iemand 'n kind uitbuit; gedrag waaraan 'n kind blootgestel word of waarvan hy die teiken is en wat hom sielkundig of emosioneel kan skaad.
items.bron: Children's Act 38 of 2005 s1, 'abuse': 'any form of harm or ill-treatment deliberately inflicted on a child', including (a) assaulting a child or inflicting any other form of deliberate injury, (b) sexually abusing a child or allowing a child to be sexually abused, (c) bullying by another child, (d) a labour practice that exploits a child, and (e) exposing or subjecting a child to behaviour that may harm the child psychologically or emotionally (DoH mandatory-reporting guide, knowledgehub.health.gov.za; lawforall.co.za). The lesson's 'grootmens' is an instance of the Act's 'allowing', which is not limited to adults. That is narrower but not false.

items.bewering: vernedering: Wanneer iemand 'n kind so behandel dat sy waardigheid as mens aangetas word, asof hy minder werd is as ander mense. Dit bly vernedering, ook wanneer die kind nie daaroor kla nie.
items.bron: 'Vernedering' corresponds to 'degradation' in s28(1)(d). Constitution s10: 'Everyone has inherent dignity and the right to have their dignity respected and protected' (en.wikisource.org Chapter 2). S v Williams (CC, 1995, Wikipedia case article) held that whipping juveniles was degrading and violated dignity as a matter of the treatment itself, not of whether the child objected. Dignity is inherent, so its violation does not depend on a complaint.

items.bewering: gesondheidsorg: Die hulp wat gesondheidswerkers gee om 'n mens gesond te hou, gesond te maak of te help leef met iets wat nie weggaan nie. 'n Dokter, 'n verpleegster, 'n tandarts, 'n apteker en baie ander doen daardie werk.
items.bron: WHO, Universal Health Coverage fact sheet (who.int): health services span 'health promotion to prevention, treatment, rehabilitation and palliative care'. Keeping healthy, making healthy and living with a lasting condition map onto that range.

items.bewering: maatskaplike dienste: die hulp vir 'n kind of 'n gesin wat swaarkry of nie veilig is nie; dit is die staat se werk om te sorg dat daardie hulp daar is; maatskaplike werkers bring baie daarvan, en ander opgeleide werkers help ook; organisasies wat die staat vir hierdie werk aangewys het, lewer ook hierdie dienste.
items.bron: Constitution s28(1)(c), a child's right to social services (source.acts.co.za). Children's Act s105 says designated child protection services may be provided by the national or provincial Department of Social Development or by a designated organisation. Under s107 the Director-General or provincial head designates child protection organisations (acts.co.za s105, s107, reg. 31). Designated social workers investigate under s155.

items.bewering: onderhandelinge: Gesprekke waarin mense saam na 'n ooreenkoms soek.
items.bron: This is the ordinary meaning of negotiation. In context it refers to the CODESA constitutional negotiations named in the charter's preamble (naturalchild.org). The negotiations sought agreement on a new constitution (AAM Archives pro25).

opsomming: Every historical, constitutional and legal claim checked out against sources, including the 1992 summit, the Charter's articles, all seven section 28 items, s2, s7, s8, s36, and the Children's Act definitions of abuse and neglect; a person must decide on one glossary sentence, 'Armoede alleen is nie verwaarlosing nie', because the Children's Act does not say it and the SA Law Reform Commission treats neglect caused by lack of resources as a recognised kind of neglect.
